stem: According to the passage, how can trees help manage rainwater?
options: Their leaves and branches intercept rain, while roots help water soak into soil.
Their roots direct rainfall quickly into city drains during heavy showers.
Their canopies prevent rain from reaching pavements and underground services.
Their leaves absorb all rainfall before it can contribute to urban flooding.

verdicts.working: The passage says leaves and branches intercept some rainfall, while roots and soil help water soak into the ground.

working: The passage states that leaves and branches intercept some rainfall and roots and surrounding soil allow more water to soak into the ground.
solution: Leaves and branches intercept some rainfall, while roots and surrounding soil help water soak into the ground.
